translation.english_title: A kurinji flower sways and calls

english_lines: Aa-aa... aaaa... laalalaa...
A kurinji flower sways and calls,
Come, cool breeze, to mingle and play,
In the breeze's pleasure, honey-waist mingling,
Let us live as tender shoots, floating in delight.
notes: The opening vocalization is retained rather than replaced by new English vocables.
`குறிஞ்சி` remains `kurinji`, preserving the culture-bearing landscape/flower term.
The compact `தேனிடை` is kept as the source-shaped image `honey-waist`; it is not generalized into sweetness or beauty.

english_lines: In the rock-candy garden, milk flowing,
Driving the plough with sugarcane as the ploughshare,
O grain-gem, wondrously grown,
O grain-gem, wondrously grown,
Let us embrace and rejoice, eye-gem!
(Kurinji).
notes: Rock-candy garden, milk, sugarcane-plough and `கதிர்மணி` remain an agricultural-sweetness image-chain rather than being collapsed into a conventional compliment.
The repeated `அற்புதமாய் விளைந்த கதிர்மணியே` remains repeated.

source_tamil_lines: இயல் இசை கூத்தென முத்தமிழ் சுவையை தருக
english_lines: Come write a preface for the tongue of pleasure,
Give the taste of Muthamizh — iyal, isai, koothu,
Muthamizh, fish-eyed one — your speech is the three fruits,
You are a path to mukti,
Pour a pearl-rain.
notes: `இயல் / இசை / கூத்து` and `முத்தமிழ்` remain culturally audible as `iyal / isai / koothu / Muthamizh` rather than being flattened into generic literature, music and drama.
`முக்கனி` remains `the three fruits`, preserving the Tamil cultural image; `முத்தி` remains `mukti`.
`முத்துமாரி` is represented as `pearl-rain`, retaining the source's `muthu/maari` image rather than replacing it with generic blessing.

english_lines: If embraced, the two lamps will go out,
The trembling body will grow faint,
If Tamil Mother joins us,
From now on, never will I part from you,
(Kurinji).
notes: `அணைத்தால்` carries the source's embrace/extinguish pressure; `the two lamps will go out` is retained without inventing an explanatory body-part gloss.
`தமிழன்னை` remains `Tamil Mother`, and the final joined source form `நானுன்னை` is translated without altering the Tamil witness.

translator_notes: The duet moves through kurinji, agricultural sweetness, Muthamizh and Tamil Mother while keeping erotic imagery active; the English retains those layers instead of separating them into explanatory prose.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
